subject: Sentinel Health — API behavior contracts: streaming, tokenization, and schema decisions

Subject: Sentinel Health — API behavior contracts: streaming, tokenization, and schema decisions

Hi Emma — great call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so the eng teams can unblock: 

1) Objective: narrow the contract for request/response behavior so Sentinel can start implementation in parallel with our Dedicated eval. Key buckets: auth & SDK bootstrap, routing & tenant selection, structured/tool-calling semantics, embeddings/reranker integration, and request/response knobs (chat vs completions, tokenization, max_tokens, stop sequences, streaming).

2) Constraints you mentioned on the call:
- On-prem proxy between Sentinel’s VPC and Redwood Private (mutual TLS + client certs).
- Must support streaming for transcription assist UI without buffering >200ms on our side.
- Need deterministic token accounting for billing and safety checks — tokenization must be reproducible by their pipeline.

3) Proposed initial decisions (for discussion):
- SDK: recommend using Redwood JS SDK v2 for client bootstrap. Support both API-key and mTLS auth; client will pass a tenant-id header for routing.
- Auth: mTLS for private deployment; API keys + role-scoped key for hosted dev. We’ll provide an example Node bootstrap that includes key rotation hooks.
- Routing: tenant-id + region hints in header; if tenant pinned to Dedicated pool, requests route to Dedicated. Fallback policy documented (see attached checklist).
- Structured output/tool calling: return JSON blocks under "tools" field; SDK will emit a parser which validates shape. We’ll provide suggested schema (attached suggested-schema.md).
- Embeddings/reranker: embeddings call separate endpoint; we recommend offline reranking by computing dense vectors then a rerank call using a lightweight scoring API.
- Chat vs completions: recommend chat for multi-turn assistant workflows (preserve state/KV cache) and completions for single-shot generation. Important to define the chunking policy and how max_tokens applies (prompt vs response).
- Tokenization: we will include a tokenization utility (deterministic BPE) in SDK; we need you to confirm any pre-tokenization or text normalization you do (e.g., strip markup) so counts match.
- Streaming semantics: stream tokens as they are produced with incremental commit events. Provide an option to get only final json-blocks (non-stream) for strict schema validation, and a streaming-json mode for the UI.

Next steps: can you confirm the security contact for cert exchange and whether your infra team requires a pre-signed client cert or will run their own CA? Also please review the attached integration-checklist.xlsx and suggested-schema.md and flag anything that blocks.

Thanks — I’ve looped Laura for commercial/contract notes and Karthik for SDK & runtime specifics.

—
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — this is helpful. A few clarifying points from our infra side after grooming: 

- Cert exchange: we will run our own internal CA and will provide a CA bundle; prefer client certs issued by our CA. We expect Redwood to accept client-presented certs and validate against our bundle.
- Streaming latency: our target is <150ms end-to-end for short tokens in the UI. Can you confirm Redwood’s batching behavior will not introduce artificial hold times beyond a 50ms scheduling window? We need a guarantee or an SLA note for the Dedicated eval.
- Tokenization: we already normalize newline handling and strip HTML on our side. We will forward raw text + a normalized flag if helpful. We need the SDK tokeniser to match exactly (same BPE vocab + unicode normalization).
- Max tokens: for the assist flows we want the response budget to be enforced server-side (to prevent runaway costs). Is there a way to set separate prompt_token_limit and response_token_limit in the request? That will let us cap model output without truncating upstream context.

Also: when you say "streaming-json mode" — can the SDK provide a reconstructable stream that emits both partial tokens and structured tool-call events (e.g., {event: "tool_call", name: "search", args: {...}}) so we can render partial UI and prefetch tool results?

We'll scan the attachments and follow up with a couple of acceptance-test prompts.

—Emma

Emma — thanks for the specifics. Short answers inline: 

- mTLS: yes — Redwood Private will allow you to present client certs from your CA bundle; we’ll coordinate the trust store update during onboarding.
- Batching/latency: our Dedicated scheduler has a configurable scheduling window; default is 50ms. For the eval we can set the window to 20ms for your tenant to meet the <150ms E2E target, assuming your front-end processes tokens as they arrive. I’ll get Karthik to include the scheduler knob in the checklist.
- Tokenization utilities: the SDK will include the exact tokenizer (BPE vocab v1.2) and an explicit normalization flag. If you send "normalized=true" we’ll skip normalization server-side. We’ll attach the exact tokenizer manifest.
- Prompt vs response caps: we support prompt_token_limit and response_token_limit; you can set both. If model would exceed response_token_limit, the server truncates and emits a "response_truncated" event in the stream.
- Streaming-json mode: yes — stream frames will include token frames and semantic frames. Token frames: {type:"token", text:"..."}. Semantic frames: {type:"tool_call", name:"search", args:{...}, partial:true/false}. The SDK exposes a high-level event handler so your UI can render partial tokens and prefetch tool results.

I’ve attached proposed-contract-apis.pdf with the frame shape and an updated integration checklist.

Action items: 
- Emma: confirm cert process and share CA bundle by Wed 8/26.
- Sentinel DevOps: review scheduler knob and agree to 20ms window for eval.
- Laura: I think we can offer a limited SLA note for the Dedicated eval around scheduling window. Laura, can you propose language we can send to legal?

Ben
